- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward — reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., > 0.3) and price is rising, model often overshoots — cap forecast peaks or adjust downward slightly after spike.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30d forecasts when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — add 1–2% buffer to forecast for such cases.
- Model overestimates in late 30d forecasts when sentiment is negative — reduce final 5–7 days of forecast by 1–3% to align with mean reversion.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, model often fails to capture the rebound — add 1–2% upward adjustment in the first 3–5 days of forecast.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model tends to lag — delay peak forecast by 1–3 days and smooth transitions.
- Model often ignores sentiment when price is near historical mean — if sentiment is neutral, apply slight mean reversion bias toward recent 7-day average.
